title: Buy equipment on credit
prompt: The business buys a laptop for 2,000 on 30 days' credit. Ignore sales tax.
hint: An asset goes up and so does a liability.
explanation: Equipment (asset) increases with a debit; Accounts Payable (liability) increases with a credit.

title: Invoice a customer
prompt: You invoice a customer 5,000 for consulting work finished this month. Ignore sales tax.
hint: Revenue is earned when the work is done, not when cash arrives.
explanation: Accounts Receivable (asset) up with a debit; Sales (revenue) up with a credit.

title: Customer pays an invoice
prompt: The customer pays the 5,000 invoice from last month into the bank.
hint: The revenue was already recognised; one asset swaps for another.
explanation: Bank up (debit), Accounts Receivable down (credit). Crediting Sales again would double count.

title: Owner takes money out
prompt: A sole trader transfers 1,000 from the business account to their personal account.
hint: This is not an expense of the business.
explanation: Drawings reduce equity (debit Owner Drawings) and the bank goes down (credit Bank).

title: Repay a loan instalment
prompt: A loan instalment of 1,200 is paid: 1,000 principal and 200 interest.
hint: Split the payment: only one part is an expense.
explanation: Principal reduces the Loan liability; interest is an expense. Bank goes down by the full 1,200.

title: Pay a year of insurance upfront
prompt: On 1 January the business pays 1,200 for 12 months of insurance. Record the payment.
hint: The cover has not been used yet.
explanation: The whole amount is a Prepayment (asset) until each month of cover is used.

title: Release one month of insurance
prompt: At 31 January, release one month of the 1,200 insurance prepayment.
explanation: Insurance expense 100 (debit), Prepayments down 100 (credit).

title: Accrue an unbilled expense
prompt: At 31 March, electricity used in March is estimated at 300 (net of tax). The bill arrives in April.
hint: The cost belongs to March; nothing has been billed yet.
explanation: Utilities expense (debit) and Accrued Expenses liability (credit). Reverse it on 1 April.

title: Post depreciation
prompt: Equipment costing 3,000 with no residual value is depreciated straight line over 3 years. Post one year.
hint: The credit does not go to the asset's cost account.
explanation: Depreciation expense 1,000 (debit); Accumulated Depreciation (contra-asset) 1,000 (credit).

title: Raise an allowance for credit losses
prompt: At year end you estimate 600 of receivables will not be collected.
hint: Use the contra-asset, not the receivable itself.
explanation: Bad Debts expense (debit) and Allowance for Credit Losses (credit). Specific write-offs later use the allowance.

title: Write stock down to NRV
prompt: Damaged stock that cost 1,000 can now only be sold for 600.
hint: Lower of cost and net realisable value.
explanation: Write down by 400: Inventory Write-down expense (debit), Inventory (credit).

title: Annual subscription received upfront
prompt: A customer pays 12,000 for a 12-month subscription starting today.
hint: Nothing has been delivered yet.
explanation: Cash in (debit Bank), Deferred Revenue liability (credit). Release 1,000 to Sales each month.

title: Sell an old asset at a loss
prompt: Equipment cost 10,000 with 7,000 accumulated depreciation is sold for 2,500 cash. Ignore tax.
hint: Remove both the cost and the accumulated depreciation.
explanation: Carrying amount 3,000 less proceeds 2,500 = loss of 500.

title: Start an IFRS 16 lease
prompt: A lessee signs a 5-year lease. The present value of the lease payments is 50,000. No payment yet.
hint: Two new balance sheet lines.
explanation: Right-of-Use Asset (debit) and Lease Liability (credit) at the present value.

title: Buy a laptop with GST
prompt: An Australian business buys a laptop for $2,200 including GST on credit, with a tax invoice.
hint: GST is 1/11 of the inclusive price.
explanation: Computer Equipment $2,000, GST credit $200 (debit to the GST account), Accounts Payable $2,200.

title: Invoice with GST
prompt: Invoice a customer $1,100 including GST for services.
hint: Sales are recorded net of GST.
explanation: Accounts Receivable $1,100; Sales $1,000; GST collected $100 (credit to the GST account).

title: Pay the BAS
prompt: The BAS shows 1A $100 and 1B $20. Pay the net GST.
hint: Clear the GST account.
explanation: Paying $80 debits the GST liability and credits the bank.

title: Run payroll
prompt: Gross wages $2,000, PAYG withheld $300, net pay $1,700 paid from the bank.
hint: Expense the gross; withholding is owed to the ATO.
explanation: Wages expense at gross; PAYG Withholdings Payable $300; Bank $1,700.

title: Accrue super
prompt: Accrue super guarantee at 12% on $2,000 of qualifying earnings.
hint: Super is paid on top of wages.
explanation: Superannuation expense $240 and Superannuation Payable $240. No GST.

title: Invoice with VAT
prompt: Invoice a UK client £1,000 plus VAT at the standard rate.
hint: VAT is added on top of the net price.
explanation: Trade Debtors £1,200; Sales £1,000; VAT £200.

title: Buy supplies with VAT
prompt: Buy office supplies for £120 including VAT on account, with a VAT invoice.
hint: VAT is 1/6 of a gross price.
explanation: Office Expenses £100; VAT reclaimable £20; Trade Creditors £120.

title: Post a UK payroll journal
prompt: Gross pay £3,000; PAYE £300; employee NIC £120; employer NIC £387.45 (15% of the pay above the £417 monthly threshold); employee pension £120; employer pension £90.
hint: Net pay is gross less PAYE, employee NIC and employee pension.
explanation: PAYE & NIC Payable = 300 + 120 + 387.45; Pensions Payable = 120 + 90; net pay = 3,000 − 300 − 120 − 120 = 2,460.

title: Subcontractor bill under CIS
prompt: A verified subcontractor (not VAT registered) invoices £2,000 labour and £500 materials. CIS at 20%.
hint: Deduct from labour only.
explanation: Cost £2,500; CIS Deductions Payable £400 (20% × £2,000); owed to the subcontractor £2,100.
